title: Condition
description: A binary state container applied/removed by effects from the shared effect registry. Each condition is an 'envelope' that a consuming effect (e.g. paralyze, poison) fills when applied to a target. Conditions do not define their own mechanics inline — they reference effect IDs that apply or remove them.

label.description: Human-readable name with spaces and capitalization.

description.description: What the condition is and what it does at a glance.

effects.description: Narrative/descriptive effects of this condition in each resolution mode.

video_game.description: Mechanical effect in video game/action-combat mode.

appliedBy.description: Effect refs that can apply this condition. Use namespaced format core:effect/<key> or bare key.

removedBy.description: Effect refs that can remove this condition (typically core:effect/cure). May be empty for conditions with only non-effect removal (e.g. prone is removed by the 'stand' action, not by any effect).

stacking.description: Whether multiple instances of this condition stack (e.g. exhaustion has 6 levels).

maxStacks.description: Maximum stack count if stacking is true.

combat.description: Combat mechanics this condition applies to its bearer. All fields are optional; omit for conditions with no direct combat impact (e.g. charmed, deafened, silenced).

attack_penalty.description: Flat penalty applied to the bearer's attack rolls while this condition is active. Example: prone → −20.

defense_bonus.description: Flat bonus TO attackers' rolls against the bearer while this condition is active. Example: blinded → +10 to attackers.

prevents_action.description: If true, the bearer cannot take any actions, bonus actions, or reactions. Example: paralyzed, stunned.

auto_crit_when_target.description: If true, melee attacks against the bearer automatically become critical hits. Example: paralyzed, unconscious.

attack_penalty_per_stack.description: Per-stack penalty applied to attack rolls. Only meaningful for stacking conditions like exhaustion (e.g. −10 per stack = −30 at 3/6). The resolver multiplies this by the current stack count.
